detail.text: The interior theorem rests on two published inputs with no Lean counterpart. The distance estimate (Prop 1.9) comes from the equidistribution estimate Prop 1.12: sums over primes p in [P,2P] of e(N/p + M/p^j) match their integral up to O(P log^{-A} P), proved with Vaughan's identity and a Vinogradov-type exponential-sum bound (their §4). The Kane-type estimate (Prop 1.10) comes from derivative estimates for the function f_t with C(f_t(m), m) = t (Prop 2.1, via the digamma function and Stirling)…

route.text: Decompose along MRSTT 2022 §1.2 (Thm 1.3 strategy): maximal-k interior solution; every other interior solution within exp((log log a)^(9/10)) of it (Prop 1.9 with (1.5), (1.7)); Kane-type estimate Prop 1.10 allows at most one such neighbour. Assembly proved (PR #1058); the two holes are the paper's propositions.

references.note: Theorem 1.3: for every ε > 0 and t sufficiently large depending on ε, C(n,m) = t has at most two solutions with exp(log^{2/3+ε} n) ≤ m ≤ n/2; take ε = 1/6. Remark 1.4: two is attained infinitely often (Lind's family). Remark 1.7: the threshold is effective but unoptimised.
references.title: K. Matomäki, M. Radziwiłł, X. Shao, T. Tao, J. Teräväinen, Singmaster's conjecture in the interior of Pascal's triangle, Quart. J. Math. 73 (2022) 1137–1177

literature_proposed.summary: Known (2022), not formalised: for every sufficiently large a, at most two rows n hold a with exp((log n)^{5/6}) ≤ k ≤ n/2. This is Theorem 1.3 of Matomäki–Radziwiłł–Shao–Tao–Teräväinen with ε = 1/6 (they count solutions (n,k); each row of this set gives one, so rows ≤ solutions ≤ 2). The proof uses equidistribution of fractional parts over random primes and Kane-type estimates (their Propositions 1.9, 1.10, 1.12); far from Mathlib. Two is attained (Lind's C(104,39) = C(103,40) lies in this region in both rows).
